about.architecture.domain: Pure TypeScript domain functions are separated from React Native components.
about.architecture.i18n: All clinical and interface copy is resolved through English and Portuguese dictionaries.
about.architecture.modules: A module registry drives the home screen and route list.
about.architecture.tests: Deterministic tests cover thresholds, edge cases, classification branches, and translation parity.
about.architectureDescription: Each radiology section owns its domain rules, screens, tests, and reference content.
about.assumptionsText: Where a source uses discretionary wording, RadRef presents the source language and flags the operational assumption. In Lung-RADS, slow-growing solid or part-solid nodules are conservatively assigned 4B because v2022 states they may be classified as 4B.
about.cardDescription: Guideline versions, offline behavior, assumptions, and educational-use notice.
about.guideline.bosniak: Bosniak Classification of Cystic Renal Masses, version 2019.
about.guideline.brock: Brock/PanCan full malignancy-risk model from McWilliams et al., 2013.
about.guideline.cua: Canadian Urological Association guideline for cystic renal lesions, 2023 update.
about.guideline.fleischner: Fleischner Society recommendations for incidental pulmonary nodules, 2017.
about.guideline.lungRads: ACR Lung-RADS assessment categories and management recommendations, version 2022.
about.guidelinesDescription: The rules are identified by source and version so future updates can be isolated by module.
about.offline.externalReferences: Internet access is used only when the user opens an external reference link.
about.offline.localRules: No server is required for the clinical logic or saved language preference.
about.offline.noAccount: The app does not require an account or transmit patient data. Do not enter identifying information.
about.offlineDescription: All calculations and classifications run locally on the device.

disclaimer.short: Educational reference tool; it does not replace clinical judgment.
disclaimer.text: RadRef supports qualified healthcare professionals. It does not replace image review, clinical judgment, multidisciplinary discussion, local policy, or the original publications.
disclaimer.title: Educational reference only
home.availableModulesDescription: Choose a clinical reference section. New modules can be added without changing the existing domain engines.
lung.brock.notStandaloneManagement: Do not use the Brock percentage as a stand-alone diagnosis or management order. Integrate it with guideline context and clinical judgment.
lung.brock.note.applicability: The model was developed in a screening cohort and should not be used without considering population, prior cancer, symptoms, and local validation.
lung.brock.note.notManagement: A probability estimate does not by itself determine follow-up, biopsy, or treatment.
lung.brock.note.operationalThresholds: The <5%, 5% to <65%, and ≥65% bands are operational thresholds used in some management pathways; they are not intrinsic output categories of the original regression model.
lung.brock.prefillNotice: Diameter, type, and the minimum count were prefilled from Lung-RADS. Confirm every field; for multiple nodules, enter the actual count before interpreting risk.
lung.brock.scopeText: The Brock full model estimates malignancy probability for CT-detected nodules using the published PanCan coefficients. Validate that the population and clinical setting are appropriate before applying it.
lung.brock.sex: Sex used by the published model
lung.fleischner.inputDescription: Measurements are rounded to the nearest whole millimeter before the guideline threshold is applied.
lung.fleischner.measurementReminder: Measure the average of the long- and short-axis diameters in the plane where the nodule is largest. Thin-section CT and comparison with prior examinations remain essential.
lung.fleischner.multipleDominantNote: For multiple nodules, subsequent management is guided by the most suspicious nodule.
lung.fleischner.note.gt8Individualize: Select among short-interval CT, PET/CT, and tissue sampling according to probability of malignancy, morphology, comorbidity, and patient preference.
lung.fleischner.note.manageMostSuspiciou: Manage according to the most suspicious nodule rather than only the largest nodule.
lung.fleischner.note.optionalRiskFactors: Optional follow-up depends on morphology, upper-lobe location, and overall clinical risk.
lung.fleischner.note.partSolidHighlySusp: A persistent part-solid nodule with a solid component of 6 mm or more is highly suspicious.
lung.fleischner.note.partSolidPetLimit: PET sensitivity is limited for small solid components; tissue sampling or resection may be more appropriate when suspicion is high.
lung.fleischner.note.subsolidFiveYears: Persistent subsolid nodules require longer surveillance, generally through 5 years.
lung.fleischner.note.subsolidPersistence: A short-interval examination is used to confirm persistence because transient inflammatory subsolid nodules are common.
lung.fleischner.rec.multipleGgoGe6: CT at 3–6 months; subsequent management is based on the most suspicious nodule.
lung.fleischner.rec.multipleGgoLt6: CT at 3–6 months; if stable, consider CT at 2 and 4 years in selected high-risk patients.
lung.fleischner.rec.multiplePartSolid: CT at 3–6 months; subsequent management is based on the most suspicious nodule.
lung.fleischner.rec.multipleSolidGe6High: CT at 3–6 months, then CT at 18–24 months.
lung.fleischner.rec.multipleSolidGe6Low: CT at 3–6 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months.
lung.fleischner.rec.singleGgoGe6: CT at 6–12 months to confirm persistence, then CT every 2 years until 5 years.
lung.fleischner.rec.singlePartSolidSolid: CT at 3–6 months to confirm persistence. Persistent solid component of 6 mm or more is highly suspicious; further diagnostic evaluation should be individualized.
CT at 3–6 months to confirm persistence; consider PET/CT, tissue sampling, or resection.
CT at 3–6 months to confirm persistence; if unchanged and the solid component remains below 6 mm, annual CT for 5 years.
lung.fleischner.rec.singleSolid6to8High: CT at 6–12 months, then CT at 18–24 months.
lung.fleischner.rec.singleSolid6to8Low: CT at 6–12 months, then consider CT at 18–24 months.
lung.fleischner.rec.singleSolidGt8: Consider CT at 3 months, PET/CT, or tissue sampling.
lung.fleischner.scopeNote: Confirm the 2017 Fleischner scope: incidental finding, age 35 years or older, no known primary cancer, and no immunocompromised state.
lung.fleischner.scopeText: For incidentally detected nodules in adults 35 years or older. It is not intended for lung cancer screening, known primary cancer, or immunocompromised patients.
lung.fleischner.singleContextNote: Recommendation for a single nodule; individualize according to morphology, comorbidity, and patient preference.
lung.form.diameterHelper: Enter the measured mean diameter before rounding.
lung.form.multipleNodulesDescription: Use the most suspicious nodule to guide management when applicable.
lung.form.risk.highDescription: Older age, heavy smoking, emphysema/fibrosis, spiculation, and upper-lobe location support higher risk.
lung.form.risk.lowDescription: Younger age, limited smoking exposure, smooth morphology, and non-upper-lobe location support lower risk.
lung.home.keyPoint.incidentalVsScreening: Confirm whether the examination is incidental or part of a formal screening program.
lung.home.keyPoint.local: Apply local protocols, patient preferences, comorbidity, and multidisciplinary judgment.
lung.home.keyPoint.measurement: Use the guideline-specific measurement method and compare with the oldest relevant prior study.
lung.home.toolsDescription: Each tool has an independent domain engine and can be tested or updated separately.
lung.lungRads.additionalSuspiciousDescri: Examples include spiculation, lymphadenopathy, or other features that increase suspicion beyond size alone.
lung.lungRads.benignAirwaySecretionsDesc: Air bubbles, dependent material, fluid attenuation, or multiplicity without an underlying soft-tissue nodule.
lung.lungRads.benignJuxtapleuralDescript: Smooth oval, lentiform, or triangular nodule with a broad pleural or fissural attachment.
lung.lungRads.cyst.change.growingCysticC: Growing cystic component of a thick-walled cyst
lung.lungRads.cyst.change.growingMultilo: Increase in size of a multilocular cyst
lung.lungRads.cystDescription: Thin-walled unilocular cysts are not classified as atypical pulmonary cysts. Classify any associated nodule by its most concerning feature.
lung.lungRads.growth.description: Lung-RADS defines growth as an increase greater than 1.5 mm in mean diameter within 12 months. Longer intervals require manual longitudinal review.
lung.lungRads.growth.enterValues: Enter current diameter, prior diameter, and interval.
lung.lungRads.growth.growing: Growth criterion met: increase of {{delta}} mm over {{days}} days.
lung.lungRads.growth.invalidValues: Use positive numeric measurements and a positive interval.
lung.lungRads.growth.manualReview: Change: {{delta}} mm over {{days}} days. The interval exceeds 12 months; review all prior studies for slow growth rather than applying the 12-month binary rule.
lung.lungRads.growth.stable: Growth criterion not met: change of {{delta}} mm over {{days}} days.
lung.lungRads.growth.title: Growth helper
lung.lungRads.inflammatoryDescription: Use category 0 with short-interval follow-up when the pattern is indeterminate and likely inflammatory.
lung.lungRads.management.0Comparison: Obtain and compare prior chest CT examinations before assigning a final category.
lung.lungRads.management.0Incomplete: Obtain additional images or complete the examination as needed.
lung.lungRads.management.0Inflammatory: Consider low-dose CT in 1–3 months to assess suspected infectious or inflammatory findings.
lung.lungRads.management.1: Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.
lung.lungRads.management.2: Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.
lung.lungRads.management.4A: Low-dose CT in 3 months. PET/CT may be considered when the solid nodule or solid component is 8 mm or larger.
lung.lungRads.management.4B: Diagnostic chest CT with or without contrast; PET/CT may be considered when the solid nodule or solid component is 8 mm or larger. Consider tissue sampling and/or referral for further clinical evaluation.
lung.lungRads.management.4X: Manage as category 4 according to the most suspicious feature, with multidisciplinary evaluation as appropriate.
lung.lungRads.measurementDescription: Enter either mean diameter or volume. Volume is converted to an equivalent spherical diameter for threshold logic.
lung.lungRads.noRiskPercentages: Lung-RADS v2022 removed the malignancy-risk percentage column. RadRef therefore does not display legacy category percentages.
lung.lungRads.note.airwayBenignSecretion: Features favor benign airway secretions rather than an endobronchial soft-tissue nodule.
lung.lungRads.note.airwayPersistent: A persistent segmental or more proximal airway nodule is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.airwayResolved: The previously described airway nodule has resolved.
lung.lungRads.note.airwaySegmentalBaseli: A baseline or new segmental/proximal airway nodule is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.airwaySubsegmental: A subsegmental airway nodule is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.awaitingComparison: A final category should be assigned after comparison with prior chest CT.
lung.lungRads.note.baselinePartSolidLt6: A baseline part-solid nodule smaller than 6 mm is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.baselinePartSolidSoli: A baseline part-solid nodule with a solid component from 6 to less than 8 mm is category 4A.
A baseline part-solid nodule with a solid component of 8 mm or more is category 4B.
A baseline part-solid nodule at least 6 mm with a solid component smaller than 6 mm is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.baselineSolid6to8: A baseline solid nodule from 6 to less than 8 mm is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.baselineSolid8to15: A baseline solid nodule from 8 to less than 15 mm is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.baselineSolidGe15: A baseline solid nodule measuring 15 mm or more is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.baselineSolidLt6: A baseline solid nodule smaller than 6 mm is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.cystAssociatedNodule: The final category is the more concerning of the atypical cyst feature and the associated nodule.
lung.lungRads.note.cystGrowingCysticComp: Growth of the cystic component of a thick-walled cyst is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.cystGrowingMultilocul: Increase in size of a multilocular cyst is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.cystGrowingWallOrNodu: Increasing wall thickness or nodularity is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.cystIncreasedLoculati: Increased loculation or new/increased opacity is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.cystMultilocularBasel: A baseline multilocular cyst, or a cyst that becomes multilocular, is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.cystNoThinWalledClass: Thin-walled unilocular cysts are not classified as atypical pulmonary cysts.
lung.lungRads.note.cystStableStepDown: A stable atypical pulmonary cyst after short-term follow-up is managed as category 3 in this implementation.
lung.lungRads.note.cystThickWalledBaseli: A baseline or new thick-walled cyst is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.definitelyBenign: The finding has a definitely benign calcification pattern or macroscopic fat.
lung.lungRads.note.ggoGe30BaselineOrNew: A baseline or new non-solid nodule measuring 30 mm or more is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.ggoGe30Stable: A non-solid nodule measuring 30 mm or more that is stable or slow-growing is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.ggoLt30: A non-solid nodule smaller than 30 mm is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.growingPartSolidNoSol: A growing part-solid nodule without qualifying solid-component growth meets category 4A criteria.
lung.lungRads.note.growingPartSolidSolid: A growing part-solid nodule with a solid component of 8 mm or more meets category 4B criteria.
lung.lungRads.note.growingSolidComponent: A growing solid component measuring 4 mm or more meets category 4B criteria.
A growing solid component smaller than 4 mm meets category 4A criteria.
lung.lungRads.note.growingSolidGe8: A growing solid nodule measuring 8 mm or more meets category 4B criteria.
lung.lungRads.note.growingSolidLt8: A growing solid nodule smaller than 8 mm meets category 4A criteria.
lung.lungRads.note.incomplete: The examination or required imaging information is incomplete.
lung.lungRads.note.inflammatory: Findings may represent infection or inflammation; short-interval reassessment is appropriate when clinically indicated.
lung.lungRads.note.juxtapleuralBenign: A smooth oval, lentiform, or triangular juxtapleural nodule smaller than 10 mm is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.multipleMostSuspiciou: For multiple findings, report the category of the most suspicious lesion.
lung.lungRads.note.newPartSolidLt6: A new part-solid nodule smaller than 6 mm is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.newPartSolidSolidGe4: A new part-solid nodule with a solid component of 4 mm or more is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.newPartSolidSolidLt4: A new part-solid nodule with a solid component smaller than 4 mm is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.newSolid4to6: A new solid nodule from 4 to less than 6 mm is category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.newSolid6to8: A new solid nodule from 6 to less than 8 mm is category 4A.
lung.lungRads.note.newSolidGe8: A new solid nodule measuring 8 mm or more is category 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.newSolidLt4: A new solid nodule smaller than 4 mm is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.resolved: The previously described nodule has resolved.
lung.lungRads.note.sModifier: Append the S modifier for a clinically significant finding unrelated to lung cancer; manage that finding separately.
lung.lungRads.note.slowGrowingPartSolid4: A part-solid nodule demonstrating slow growth over multiple examinations is classified conservatively as 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.slowGrowingSolid4B: A solid nodule demonstrating slow growth over multiple screening examinations is classified conservatively as 4B.
lung.lungRads.note.solidComponentResolve: The solid component has resolved; the remaining non-solid component is category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.stepDown3to2: A category 3 solid nodule that is stable at 6-month follow-up is stepped down to category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.stepDown4Ato3: A category 4A solid nodule that is stable at 3-month follow-up is stepped down to category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.stepDownPartSolid3to2: A category 3 part-solid nodule stable at short-term follow-up is stepped down to category 2.
lung.lungRads.note.stepDownPartSolid4Ato: A category 4A part-solid nodule stable at short-term follow-up is stepped down to category 3.
lung.lungRads.note.upgradedTo4X: Additional suspicious features upgrade the finding to category 4X.
lung.lungRads.openBrock: Open Brock calculation with these measurements
lung.lungRads.sModifierDescription: The S modifier does not change the nodule category or its management.
lung.lungRads.scopeText: Use ACR Lung-RADS v2022 for lung cancer screening CT. The category is determined by the most concerning finding, and the S modifier is separate from the nodule category.
lung.lungRads.warning.measurementRequire: A positive nodule measurement is required for this morphology.
lung.lungRads.warning.slowGrowthAssumpti: Operational assumption: v2022 states that slow-growing solid or part-solid nodules may be classified as 4B; RadRef applies 4B conservatively.

lung.references.point.brockInputs: The implemented formula uses age, sex, family history, emphysema, diameter, nodule type, upper-lobe location, nodule count, and spiculation.
lung.references.point.brockScope: The Brock full model was derived from a screening cohort and estimates risk rather than prescribing management.
lung.references.point.brockThresholds: The displayed <5%, 5% to <65%, and ≥65% bands are operational thresholds, not original regression categories.
lung.references.point.fleischnerMeasurem: Round the mean of long- and short-axis measurements to the nearest whole millimeter before applying thresholds.
lung.references.point.fleischnerPartSoli: Persistent part-solid nodules with a solid component of 6 mm or more are highly suspicious; PET may be limited for small solid components.
lung.references.point.fleischnerRisk: Risk is a clinical synthesis, not a binary property determined by smoking history alone.
lung.references.point.fleischnerScope: Use for incidental nodules in adults 35 years or older; exclude screening, known primary malignancy, and immunocompromised states.
lung.references.point.lungRadsCysts: Atypical pulmonary cyst criteria distinguish growth of the cystic component, wall/nodularity, multiloculation, and associated nodules.
lung.references.point.lungRadsGrowth: Growth is more than 1.5 mm in mean diameter within 12 months; slow growth over longer periods requires longitudinal review.
lung.references.point.lungRadsNoRiskColu: Version 2022 removed the malignancy-risk percentage column; legacy percentages should not be presented as current category definitions.
lung.references.point.lungRadsSModifier: The S modifier denotes a clinically significant non-lung-cancer finding and does not replace the nodule category.
lung.references.point.lungRadsScreening: Lung-RADS applies to screening CT, not incidental examinations.

renal.bosniak.acquisitionDescription: The selected content pattern must be compatible with the acquisition. Ultrasound alone is insufficient for full Bosniak v2019 classification.
renal.bosniak.alternativeEtiology: Suspected infectious, inflammatory, or vascular lesion
renal.bosniak.content.ctOver20Nonenhanci: Renal protocol CT: homogeneous >20 HU and nonenhancing
renal.bosniak.content.ctTooSmallLowAtten: CT: homogeneous low attenuation, too small to characterize
renal.bosniak.content.mriT1MarkedHomogen: Noncontrast MRI: markedly T1 hyperintense and homogeneous
renal.bosniak.content.mriT2CSFLike: MRI: homogeneous and CSF-like on T2
renal.bosniak.cysticMassDescription: Less than 25% of the mass should consist of enhancing tissue.
renal.bosniak.enhancingTissueHelper: Bosniak v2019 cystic mass definition: less than 25% enhancing tissue.
renal.bosniak.reason.alternativeEtiology: The suspected infectious, inflammatory, or vascular etiology is outside the Bosniak neoplastic cystic-mass pathway.
renal.bosniak.reason.calcificationObscur: Abundant thick or nodular calcification on CT can obscure enhancement.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIICalcificatio: Calcification of any type may be present in Bosniak II when it does not obscure enhancement.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIDefault: The mass meets benign Bosniak II criteria.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIEnhancingSep: One to three thin smooth enhancing septa are permitted in Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIFHeterogeneo: A heterogeneously T1-hyperintense cystic mass on unenhanced MRI qualifies as Bosniak IIF.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIFManySepta: Four or more thin smooth enhancing septa qualify as Bosniak IIF.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIFMinimalSept: A smooth enhancing septum thicker than 2 mm but thinner than 4 mm qualifies as Bosniak IIF.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIFMinimalWall: A smooth enhancing wall thicker than 2 mm but thinner than 4 mm qualifies as Bosniak IIF.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIIObtuseProtr: An enhancing obtuse-margin protrusion smaller than 4 mm represents irregular thickening and qualifies as Bosniak III.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIISeptumIrreg: An irregular enhancing septum qualifies as Bosniak III.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIIThickSeptum: An enhancing septum 4 mm or thicker qualifies as Bosniak III.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIIThickWall: Enhancing wall thickness of 4 mm or more qualifies as thick and Bosniak III.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIIIWallIrregul: An irregular enhancing wall qualifies as Bosniak III.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIINonenhancing: Any number of thin smooth nonenhancing septa may be present in Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.classISimple: Well-defined simple-fluid mass with a smooth wall 2 mm or thinner, without septa, calcification, or protrusions.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIVAcuteProtrus: An enhancing protrusion with acute margins is a nodule of any size and qualifies as Bosniak IV.
renal.bosniak.reason.classIVObtuseNodule: An enhancing protrusion with obtuse margins measuring at least 4 mm qualifies as a nodule and Bosniak IV.
renal.bosniak.reason.confirmCystic: Confirm that less than 25% of the mass consists of enhancing tissue.
renal.bosniak.reason.enhancementOnNoncon: Enhancement cannot be established on an explicitly noncontrast examination.
renal.bosniak.reason.enhancingPercentGe2: At least 25% of the mass is enhancing tissue, so it is not predominantly cystic by the Bosniak v2019 definition.
renal.bosniak.reason.hereditarySyndrome: A hereditary renal cancer syndrome requires a syndrome-specific approach.
renal.bosniak.reason.heterogeneousCtNoEn: A heterogeneous nonenhancing mass on CT may contain occult enhancing elements.
renal.bosniak.reason.incompatiblePattern: The selected special content pattern is not compatible with the selected acquisition.
renal.bosniak.reason.invalidEnhancingPer: The estimated enhancing-tissue percentage must be between 0% and 100%.
renal.bosniak.reason.noSafeClass: The entered combination does not satisfy a safe complete Bosniak v2019 branch.
renal.bosniak.reason.nonenhancingProtrus: A nonenhancing protrusion does not qualify as a Bosniak III/IV enhancing nodule.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.ctAtLeast70: Homogeneous mass of at least 70 HU on noncontrast CT is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.ctMinus9To2: Homogeneous −9 to 20 HU mass on noncontrast CT is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.ctOver20Non: Homogeneous mass greater than 20 HU without enhancement on renal protocol CT is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.ctPortal21T: Homogeneous 21–30 HU mass on portal venous phase CT is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.ctTooSmallL: Homogeneous low-attenuation mass too small to characterize on CT is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.mriT1Hetero: Heterogeneous T1 hyperintensity is evaluated under the Bosniak IIF MRI-specific criterion.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.mriT1Marked: Markedly T1-hyperintense homogeneous mass on noncontrast MRI is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.mriT2CSFLik: Homogeneous mass with cerebrospinal-fluid-like T2 signal on MRI is Bosniak II.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.none: No special benign content pattern was selected.
renal.bosniak.reason.special.simpleFluid: The content follows simple-fluid attenuation or signal.
renal.bosniak.reason.ultrasoundIncomplet: Ultrasound alone does not provide the full contrast-enhanced CT/MRI feature set required for Bosniak v2019.
renal.bosniak.report.II: Cystic renal mass with benign Bosniak II features.
renal.bosniak.report.IIF: Cystic renal mass, Bosniak IIF; imaging surveillance is recommended according to clinical context.
renal.bosniak.report.III: Cystic renal mass, Bosniak III; recommend urologic evaluation and shared decision-making.
renal.bosniak.report.IV: Cystic renal mass with enhancing nodule, Bosniak IV; recommend urologic evaluation.
renal.bosniak.report.alternativeEtiology: Bosniak v2019 is not applied because an infectious, inflammatory, or vascular etiology is suspected.
renal.bosniak.report.calcifiedIncomplete: Thick or nodular calcification may obscure enhancement on CT; MRI with subtraction is recommended before final Bosniak classification.
renal.bosniak.report.confirmCystic: Bosniak classification is deferred until the lesion is confirmed to be predominantly cystic.
renal.bosniak.report.enhancementOnNoncon: Enhancement cannot be assessed on the noncontrast examination; a Bosniak class is not assigned.
renal.bosniak.report.hereditary: Bosniak v2019 is not applied because a hereditary renal cancer syndrome requires a dedicated pathway.
renal.bosniak.report.heterogeneousCt: Heterogeneous nonenhancing appearance on CT is incompletely characterized; MRI is recommended to exclude occult enhancement.
renal.bosniak.report.incompatiblePattern: The selected content pattern is incompatible with the available acquisition; a Bosniak class is not assigned.
renal.bosniak.report.incomplete: Incomplete characterization; a Bosniak category is not assigned. Recommend appropriate contrast-enhanced renal mass imaging or targeted review.
renal.bosniak.report.indeterminate: The entered features do not support a complete Bosniak v2019 category; review technique and morphology before final reporting.
renal.bosniak.report.invalidEnhancingPer: Bosniak classification is not assigned because the estimated enhancing-tissue percentage is invalid.
renal.bosniak.report.invalidMeasurements: Bosniak classification is not assigned because one or more measurements are invalid.
renal.bosniak.report.notApplicable: The lesion is outside the scope of Bosniak v2019; recommend evaluation with the appropriate alternative pathway.
renal.bosniak.report.predominantlySolid: The lesion contains at least 25% enhancing tissue and should be evaluated as a predominantly solid renal mass rather than by Bosniak v2019.
renal.bosniak.report.ultrasoundIncomplet: Ultrasound demonstrates a cystic renal lesion, but Bosniak v2019 classification is incomplete without appropriate contrast-enhanced CT or MRI.
renal.bosniak.reportReminder: The report suggestion is a drafting aid. Describe modality, enhancement, wall/septa, calcification, protrusions, and any limitation directly in the final report.
renal.bosniak.risk.IIF: Low but nontrivial risk; imaging surveillance is appropriate. Reported malignancy estimates are affected by verification and selection bias.
renal.bosniak.risk.III: Indeterminate cystic mass with an intermediate likelihood of malignancy. Published estimates often approximate 50–60% in selected surgical cohorts and are not an individual prediction.
renal.bosniak.risk.IV: Cystic mass with a high likelihood of malignancy. Published estimates often approximate 80–90% in selected surgical cohorts and are not an individual prediction.
renal.bosniak.risk.incomplete: A reliable Bosniak category cannot be assigned from the current information.
renal.bosniak.risk.notApplicable: The lesion is outside the intended Bosniak v2019 pathway.
renal.bosniak.scopeText: Classify a predominantly cystic renal mass using contrast-enhanced CT or MRI when needed. This tool applies the most severe qualifying feature and adds guardrails for incomplete or out-of-scope cases.
renal.bosniak.warning.completeContrastSt: Complete a contrast-enhanced renal mass protocol or review subtraction imaging as appropriate.
renal.bosniak.warning.enhancingPercentMi: The enhancing-tissue percentage was not provided; confirm the mass is predominantly cystic on image review.
renal.bosniak.warning.hereditaryProtocol: Apply the relevant hereditary-syndrome surveillance and management protocol.
renal.bosniak.warning.hyperattenuatingGt: Although size is no longer a defining criterion in v2019, consider MRI for a homogeneous hyperattenuating nonenhancing mass larger than 3 cm when characterization is uncertain.
renal.bosniak.warning.mriHiddenEnhanceme: MRI is recommended before assigning a final Bosniak class.
renal.bosniak.warning.mriSubtraction: MRI with subtraction is recommended to evaluate potentially obscured enhancement.
renal.bosniak.warning.nonenhancingProtru: Confirm lack of enhancement with appropriate technique and subtraction when needed.
renal.bosniak.warning.nonenhancingSepta: Septal thickness without confirmed enhancement does not by itself establish Bosniak IIF or III.
renal.bosniak.warning.nonenhancingWall: Wall thickness without confirmed enhancement does not by itself establish Bosniak IIF or III.
renal.bosniak.warning.reviewProtocol: Review image quality, enhancement assessment, morphology, and the original v2019 definitions before assigning a class.
renal.bosniak.warning.solidMassAlgorithm: Use a solid renal mass evaluation pathway.
renal.bosniak.warning.solidWithNecrosis: A predominantly solid mass with necrosis should not be classified as a Bosniak cystic mass.
renal.bosniak.warning.ultrasoundContrast: Obtain renal mass protocol CT or MRI when classification will change management.
renal.enhancement.ctConfirmed: CT attenuation increased by at least 20 HU; quantitative enhancement is confirmed.
renal.enhancement.ctIndeterminate: CT attenuation increased by 10–19.9 HU; the result is indeterminate and may require repeat measurement or MRI.
renal.enhancement.ctNotConfirmed: CT attenuation increased by less than 10 HU; quantitative enhancement is not confirmed.
renal.enhancement.insufficient: Enter valid precontrast and postcontrast values, or indicate unequivocal visual enhancement.
renal.enhancement.mriConfirmed: MRI signal increased by at least 15%; quantitative enhancement is confirmed.
renal.enhancement.mriNotConfirmed: MRI signal increased by less than 15%; quantitative enhancement is not confirmed.
renal.enhancement.mriPositivePreRequired: The precontrast MRI signal value must be greater than zero to calculate percentage increase.
renal.enhancement.scopeText: Bosniak v2019 accepts unequivocal visual enhancement or quantitative enhancement. Use matched regions of interest and appropriate subtraction imaging when needed.
renal.enhancement.thresholdReminder: Quantitative thresholds do not correct for motion, misregistration, partial volume, pseudoenhancement, or mismatched regions of interest. Review the images.
renal.enhancement.visualConfirmed: Unequivocal visible enhancement satisfies the Bosniak v2019 enhancement requirement.
renal.enhancement.visuallyUnequivocalDes: Use only when the enhancing feature is confidently visible; otherwise quantify it.
renal.home.keyPoint.cysticDefinition: A cystic mass contains less than 25% enhancing tissue; a predominantly solid mass should follow a solid renal mass pathway.
renal.home.keyPoint.enhancement: Bosniak III and IV features require enhancement; noncontrast imaging alone cannot establish it.
renal.home.keyPoint.management: Radiologic classification and management are separate decisions; size, symptoms, comorbidity, and patient preference matter.
renal.home.toolsDescription: Classification, enhancement assessment, and management are separated to preserve the clinical workflow.
renal.management.classIIF.complexityNote: Progression in complexity is more important than size change alone.
renal.management.classIIF.evidenceNote: The optimal interval is not established by high-certainty comparative evidence.
renal.management.classIIF.followUp: First follow-up at 6–12 months, then yearly if stable; consider a total of 5 years of follow-up.
renal.management.classIII.biopsyLowYield: Biopsy of Bosniak III lesions is generally low yield because there may be no targetable solid component.
renal.management.classIIIIV.20to40Primar: Active surveillance or surgery are both suggested for lesions larger than 2 cm and up to 4 cm.
renal.management.classIIIIV.comorbidityF: Individualize imaging and symptom follow-up according to goals of care.
renal.management.classIIIIV.comorbidityN: Reassess if symptoms, rapid morphologic progression, or patient goals change.
renal.management.classIIIIV.comorbidityP: Observation is suggested when major comorbidity or limited life expectancy makes intervention unlikely to provide net benefit.
renal.management.classIIIIV.definitiveOp: Definitive treatment remains an option based on patient preference and clinical context.
renal.management.classIIIIV.evidenceCond: CUA 2023: conditional recommendation; low certainty of evidence.
renal.management.classIIIIV.evidenceVery: CUA 2023: conditional recommendation; very low certainty of evidence.
renal.management.classIIIIV.gt40Primary: Surgical excision is suggested as the preferred strategy for lesions larger than 4 cm.
renal.management.classIIIIV.le20Primary: Active surveillance is suggested as the preferred strategy for lesions 2 cm or smaller.
renal.management.classIIIIV.lowCertainty: The recommendation is conditional and based on low or very low certainty evidence.
renal.management.classIIIIV.partialNephr: When surgery is selected, partial nephrectomy is suggested when technically and oncologically feasible.
renal.management.classIIIIV.selectedSurv: Active surveillance may still be reasonable in carefully selected patients who prefer it or have elevated treatment risk.
renal.management.classIIIIV.sharedDecisi: Discuss oncologic uncertainty, renal function, surgical risk, surveillance burden, and patient preference.
renal.management.classIIIIV.sizeEvidence: CUA 2023 recommendations for Bosniak III/IV are stratified at 2 cm and 4 cm.
renal.management.classIIIIV.sizeRequired: Enter lesion size to apply the CUA 2023 size-based framework for Bosniak III/IV lesions.
renal.management.classIIIIV.surveillance: No cyst-specific schedule is supported by high-certainty evidence; use an active-surveillance protocol individualized with urology.
renal.management.classIIIIV.urologyNote: Urologic evaluation and shared decision-making are appropriate.
renal.management.classIOrII.evidence: CUA 2023: strong recommendation; moderate certainty of evidence.
renal.management.classIOrII.growthNote: Growth alone does not reclassify a simple or minimally complex cyst without new complex features.
renal.management.classIOrII.note: Intervene only if symptoms develop or another clinical indication arises.
renal.management.classIOrII.primary: No routine imaging follow-up is recommended.
renal.management.classIOrII.symptomNote: Management options for symptoms depend on location, size, and patient factors.
renal.management.classIOrII.symptomaticP: Treat only if symptoms are attributable to the cystic lesion.
renal.management.classIV.biopsyTarget: For Bosniak IV lesions with a targetable solid component, biopsy may be considered if the result would change management.
renal.management.comorbidity: Major comorbidity or limited life expectancy
renal.management.comorbidityDescription: Observation may be preferred when competing health risks outweigh potential benefit.
renal.management.incomplete.evidence: No class-specific management can be assigned from incomplete characterization.
renal.management.incomplete.noteProtocol: Obtain an appropriate renal mass CT or MRI protocol when needed.
renal.management.incomplete.noteSubtract: MRI subtraction may help when enhancement is obscured or equivocal.
renal.management.notApplicable.evidence: Management guidance is not applicable to this input.
renal.management.notApplicable.note: Use the pathway appropriate for a solid renal mass, infection/inflammation, vascular lesion, or hereditary syndrome.
renal.management.notApplicable.primary: Do not apply the Bosniak management pathway until the lesion is in scope.
renal.management.scopeText: CUA 2023 recommendations for Bosniak III and IV lesions are conditional and based on low or very low certainty evidence. Use shared decision-making and urologic evaluation.
renal.management.sharedDecisionReminder: These recommendations do not account for all surgical, oncologic, renal-function, hereditary, or patient-preference factors. Use shared decision-making.
renal.management.symptomatic: Symptoms attributable to the cystic lesion
renal.management.targetableComponentDesc: Most relevant for Bosniak IV lesions when biopsy could change management.

renal.references.point.biopsy: Biopsy may help in Bosniak IV when a solid target exists and the result changes management; yield is generally low in Bosniak III.
renal.references.point.calcification: Abundant thick or nodular calcification can obscure enhancement on CT; MRI with subtraction may be required.
renal.references.point.comorbidity: Observation is reasonable when major comorbidity or limited life expectancy outweighs intervention benefit.
renal.references.point.cysticDefinition: A cystic renal mass contains less than 25% enhancing tissue.
renal.references.point.enhancementRequir: Bosniak III and IV morphology requires enhancement; use visual or quantitative criteria.
renal.references.point.evidence: Many Bosniak III/IV management recommendations are conditional and supported by low or very low certainty evidence.
renal.references.point.heterogeneousCt: A heterogeneous nonenhancing renal mass on CT should be evaluated with MRI before final classification.
renal.references.point.iifFollowUp: CUA 2023 suggests 6–12-month follow-up in the first year, then yearly, for a total of 5 years if stable.
renal.references.point.mriPatterns: Bosniak v2019 includes modality-specific benign MRI patterns and a heterogeneous T1-hyperintense IIF pattern.
renal.references.point.noncontrast: Noncontrast imaging cannot demonstrate enhancement; do not infer Bosniak III/IV features without an appropriate contrast study.
renal.references.point.protrusions: Enhancing acute-margin protrusions of any size, or obtuse-margin protrusions ≥4 mm, qualify as IV; obtuse protrusions <4 mm qualify as III.
renal.references.point.sizeManagement: For Bosniak III/IV: active surveillance is preferred at ≤2 cm; surveillance or surgery at >2–4 cm; surgery is preferred at >4 cm.
renal.references.point.thickness: Smooth enhancing wall/septa >2 to <4 mm or many thin enhancing septa qualify as IIF; ≥4 mm or irregular enhancement qualifies as III.
renal.references.point.ultrasound: Ultrasound can identify a cystic lesion but generally cannot provide complete v2019 classification without contrast-enhanced CT or MRI.

validation.ageAtLeast18: Enter an age of at least 18 years.
validation.brockSizeRange: Enter a nodule diameter from 3 to 30 mm.
validation.noduleCountPositiveInteger: Enter a positive whole number of nodules.
validation.nonNegativeProtrusionSize: Protrusion size must be zero or greater.
validation.nonNegativeSeptaCount: The number of septa must be a nonnegative whole number.
validation.nonNegativeSeptalThickness: Septal thickness must be zero or greater.
validation.nonNegativeWallThickness: Wall thickness must be zero or greater.
validation.solidNotGreaterThanTotal: The solid component cannot be larger than the total nodule diameter.
